deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a proof begun on the previous page. Since the notes use C'' and R_*, C is presumably a C*-algebra (Grothendieck writes C). Hypotheses: C sits weakly densely in a von Neumann algebra R, and C has an approximate unit, the limits 'x→1, x∈C ftt' (filtrant, i.e. along a directed family). C'' is the bidual of C, which is a von Neumann algebra. ψ: C''→R is the normal extension of the inclusion C⊂R, dual to the restriction map R_*→C', f↦f_1. Γ ⊂ C'' and Γ_1 ⊂ R seem to be the elements that multiply C into itself on both sides, that is, the idealizers of C in C'' and in R. In modern terms these are two realizations of the multiplier (double-centralizer) algebra M(C). For a∈Γ_1, φ(a)∈C'' is the weak* limit of ax (or xa) as x→1 in C, with ⟨φ(a),f⟩ = lim⟨ax,f⟩ for f∈C'. The previous page shows ψ(Γ)⊂Γ_1 and reduces 'φψ=1 on Γ' to one lemma: an element of Γ orthogonal to R_* (one whose image in R is 0) is zero.

This page proves that lemma. Take x∈Γ with ψ(x)=0 and y∈C. Then ψ(xy)=ψ(x)y=0. Since xy∈C and C embeds in R, xy=0. This holds for all y∈C, so x=0, because the approximate unit converges weakly to 1 in C''. Hence ψ is an isomorphism of Γ onto Γ_1, with inverse φ. It remains to check ψφ=1 on Γ_1. Take u∈Γ_1 and v=φu∈C'', with ⟨v,f⟩ = lim⟨ux,f⟩ for f∈C'. Then ψv is determined by ⟨ψv,f⟩ = ⟨v,f_1⟩ for f∈R_*. Normality of f gives lim⟨ux,f⟩ = ⟨u,f⟩, so ⟨ψv,f⟩ = ⟨u,f⟩ for all f∈R_*, i.e. ψv=u. CQFD.

Result in modern language: the idealizer {a : aC⊂C, Ca⊂C} of C in its enveloping von Neumann algebra C'' is canonically isomorphic, via the normal map C''→R, to the idealizer of C in any von Neumann algebra R in which C is weakly dense. In other words the multiplier algebra M(C) does not depend on the faithful nondegenerate representation chosen.
errors: In the first displayed line the map applied should be ψ (the normal map C''→R), not φ. The argument needs ψ(xy)=ψ(x)y with ψ the identity on C; the notation φ/ψ is used inconsistently on these two pages.

The proof silently uses three facts: C→R is injective (faithful representation); the approximate unit converges weakly to 1 in C'' (nondegeneracy); and lim⟨ux,f⟩=⟨u,f⟩ for normal f, because x→1 σ-weakly in R. All three are standard but not stated on this page.
The identification of Γ, Γ_1 as idealizers is inferred from the argument (the use of xy∈C). The definitions are not visible on this or the previous page, so this reading is a reconstruction.

ideas.what: Idealizer of a C*-algebra C in a von Neumann algebra containing it weakly densely; independence of this algebra from the choice of R, identified with the idealizer in the bidual C''
ideas.modern_name: Multiplier algebra M(A) = idealizer of A in A** (equivalently in π(A)'' for any faithful nondegenerate π); double centralizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: B. E. Johnson (centralizers, 1964); R. C. Busby (double centralizers, 1968); Akemann–Pedersen–Tomiyama (multipliers of C*-algebras, 1973)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's 1957 paper 'Un résultat sur le dual d'une C*-algèbre' as far as I know; unsure

ideas.what: Using the bidual C'' as a universal von Neumann algebra with the normal extension C''→R and an approximate unit to pass between weak limits
ideas.modern_name: Universal enveloping von Neumann algebra and its normal extension property
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sherman (1950), Takeda (1954); Grothendieck used biduals of C*-algebras in 1957
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Un résultat sur le dual d'une C*-algèbre', J. Math. Pures Appl. 1957

ideas.what: Lemma: an element of the idealizer that kills C on the right is zero (nondegeneracy argument)

missed.claim: The page completes a proof (CQFD) that the idealizer of C in C'' maps isomorphically onto the idealizer of C in any von Neumann algebra in which C is weakly dense. This is a representation-independent multiplier algebra, about 15 years before Busby (1968) and Akemann–Pedersen–Tomiyama (1973), whose treatment uses exactly this bidual realization.
missed.quote: Donc ψ est un isomorphisme de Γ sur Γ_1 ... d'où ⟨ψ v, f⟩ = ⟨u, f⟩, i.e. ψ v = u. CQFD.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only. It shows Grothendieck in 1953 working with what is now M(A) in the bidual formulation. The mathematics itself is now textbook-standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean early (1953) proof that the multiplier/idealizer algebra is independent of the representation, using the bidual. This predates the standard credits (Johnson 1964, Busby 1968, APT 1973) and is an interesting priority detail. However, the result is routine by modern standards, and the reading of Γ, Γ_1 as idealizers is partly inferred.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'φ(xy) = φ(x)y = 0' should be read as the map to R (ψ). The handwriting looks like φ, but the logic requires ψ.
Underlined line: likely 'Donc ψ est un isomorphisme de Γ sur Γ_1', with 'dans' and the following clause about the inverse struck out.
'(f ∈ R_φ)' should read '(f ∈ R_*)', the predual of R, as on the previous page.
'Alors qu'il suffit de prouver' probably reads 'Reste à prouver que' / 'il suffit de prouver que ψφ = 1'.
'on a dit ici que' probably reads 'on a vu ci-dessus que'.
'φ u = v ∈ C''' plausibly 'φ u = v ∈ C''', defined by ⟨v,f⟩ = lim⟨ux,f⟩ (f∈C'); the transcription's '⟨u,f⟩' there is shorthand.
'χ ...[?]' is probably part of the struck-out text or 'Reste à voir'.
